validity.recommendation: The row is a real project that was cancelled in 2014. No change needed.
validity.researcher_notes: Wikipedia gives 2,380 km and a maximum of 63 billion cubic meters per year, the same as the sheet. The cancellation year of 2014 matches the reports of 1 December 2014.

fills.researcher_notes: A BBC News report and a Sputnik report, both from 1 December 2014, say Russia dropped the South Stream pipeline after the president announced it in Ankara. The Sputnik page says the project was cancelled. A Reuters report from the same day, which the wiki also cites, says Russia scrapped the project. The Reuters link would not pass the link check, so it is not proposed. The sheet already holds three refs for this status. These two are added beside them.

fills.researcher_notes: Eni's press release of 29 December 2014 says South Stream Transport B.V. was set up to build the offshore section of the South Stream pipeline, and that Eni sold its 20 percent stake in it to Gazprom. An Oil and Gas Journal article from 30 December 2014 says Gazprom also bought the Wintershall and EDF stakes and now owns 100 percent. The sheet listed South Stream BV, which Wikipedia says was a different Eni company, renamed Eni JPDA 11-106 BV in 2012. This row covers the whole 2,380 km system. The onshore sections were planned through national joint ventures with Gazprom, such as South Stream Bulgaria AD and South Stream Serbia AG, but no onshore pipe was built. The offshore section was the only part where construction began, so its project company is listed as owner. Gazprom PJSC is the parent company. The Parent column still shows Eni SpA and will need the ownership team to follow the new owner. The existing Wikipedia ref is replaced because it supported the old owner name.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: BBC News and Sputnik reports of 1 December 2014 say Russia dropped the South Stream project. The Reuters report of the same day says it was scrapped. No source in the wiki list shows the project revived.
